cloud.title: My quiz folder
cloud.intro: Keep your quizzes in a folder in OneDrive or Google Drive. Build a quiz at home, and the quiz laptop picks it up by itself (and the other way round). Pictures, sounds and clips go along. Export and import keep working too.
cloud.none: No quiz folder linked yet. Your quizzes stay on this computer only.
cloud.disconnectSure: Unlink the quiz folder? Your quizzes stay on this computer and in the folder, they just stop syncing.
cloud.how: Pick the same folder on every computer that runs Quizbrew. It syncs at start, every minute and right after you save. A quiz you delete, or the older one when both computers changed it, waits 30 days in the _trash folder.
cloud.notFound: That folder cannot be found. Is OneDrive or Google Drive running on this computer?
cloud.missing: The library folder inside your quiz folder is gone, so nothing was deleted. Check the folder and sync again.
cloud.absolute: Type the full path of the folder, for example C:\Users\you\OneDrive\Quizbrew.
cloud.inside: Pick a folder outside Quizbrew's own folder.
cloud.typeIt: The folder window did not open. Type the path of the folder instead.

network.title: Network not working?
network.intro: Quizbrew runs on this laptop. Phones open the address on the big screen, so they must be on the same network as this laptop, and that network must let devices talk to each other. Playing needs no internet; only the AI question maker does.

network.kind.vpn: a VPN: phones can't use this one
network.kind.virtual: a virtual network card: phones can't use this one
network.step1Text: Type the address from the big screen in the browser of this laptop. Do you see Quizbrew? Then everything runs fine and the problem is the network or the firewall. The address:
network.step2Text: Check which wifi the phone is on. Mobile data never works. Guest wifi and staff wifi are often two separate networks.
network.step3Text: Does this laptop have more than one address above? Put another one on the QR code, usually the one with wifi or network cable.
network.step4Text: A VPN on this laptop can keep phones out. Turn it off while you play.
network.step5Text: Did you click the Windows question away the first time? Let Quizbrew fix it. Windows asks for permission first: click Yes.
network.step6: Guest wifi that keeps devices apart.
network.step6Text: Many venue and café networks turn on 'client isolation': phones get internet, but cannot reach each other. Ask the venue if it can be turned off, or bring your own network (below).
network.noInternet: A phone says 'no internet'? That's fine: Quizbrew does not need internet. Tap 'Stay connected' or 'Keep wifi'.
network.fwFailed: That did not work. Did you click Yes when Windows asked for permission?
network.fwOnLaptop: Do this on the quiz laptop itself.
network.ownIntro: The venue's wifi won't play along? Make your own little network. Quizbrew keeps the game between the devices, so it needs no internet.
network.routerText: A few tens of euros, fits in your bag, handles 20 to 30 phones and works the same in every venue. Plug it in, connect this laptop and let the teams join its wifi.
network.hotspot1: Open Settings → Network & internet → Mobile hotspot.
network.hotspot2: Pick a simple name and password under Properties, and turn the hotspot on.
network.hotspot3: Let the teams join that wifi. Above, put the address that starts with 192.168.137. on the QR code.
network.hotspotLimit: Windows lets at most 8 devices join. Enough when every team shares one phone and there are few teams.
network.phoneText: Put this laptop and the teams on the hotspot of your phone. Quizbrew uses almost no data, but phones may update in the background. Most phones allow 5 to 10 devices.
error.full: The quiz is full: no more teams can join.
host.lobbyTip: No internet needed: phones only have to be on the same wifi as this laptop. Big night? Ask for one phone per team.
network.bigIntro: Quizbrew handles up to 40 teams. Three habits keep a full room smooth.
network.onePhoneText: Ask every team to answer on one phone. Fewer devices on the wifi keeps it fast, the team talks about the answer together, and there are fewer 'mine doesn't work' moments.
network.noNetText: The game stays between this laptop and the phones. Slow venue internet or no internet at all makes no difference. Say it at the start: join the wifi, ignore 'no internet'.
network.bigRouterText: A wifi 6 router that handles 100 devices or more. It needs no internet cable: plug it in, join the laptop and play.
round.wordWeb.desc: A board full of words hides groups of four. Teams find the groups on their phones and type what links each one. A point per group, a point per link.
round.wordWeb.how: Sort the words into groups of four and type what links each group. A point per group, a point per link.
